label: Whatever is IMMENSE_2 is IMMENSE_1
paraphrase: Open sense bridge, analyst formulation, unattributed. Whatever is INFINITE_1 and causes the being of every other being in act as to being (IMMENSE_2) is measured or contained by no place and present to everything that is (IMMENSE_1, the primitive Primitives.Immense). After ST I q.8 a.1-3: God is in all things as an agent is present to that on which it acts, in every place by giving it being, and present to all by essence as the cause of their being. IMMENSE_2 types only causing being (tenselessly), which q.8 a.3 gives as the ground of presence by essence. The bridge carries what IMMENSE_2 leaves untyped: place, containment and measure; presence by power and by knowledge (the other two modes of q.8 a.3); the q.8 a.1 contact principle (an agent is joined to that on which it acts), which turns causing being into being present; sustaining as against merely originating causation (conservation, q.104 a.1), which makes the presence present now, since CausesIn ... esse is tenseless (DEF-CAUSE-OF-PERFECTION); and immediacy of presence. Its antecedent does not say that the being is incorporeal, so 'contained by no place' rests on infinity alone in this bridge. Objections. (a) Existential inertia, SUBSTANTIVE: target this bridge, read with CausesIn as originating causation; mechanism: if things, once caused, persist without concurrent sustaining causation, an originating cause of the being of all need not now be present to anything; independent justification: Schmid 2021 (pinned and read in the corpus, attempt conservation-existential-inertia-rival and docs/eternity-dependence-connection.md) explains persistence by earlier existence plus the absence of destructive causal change; relevance: the bridge itself carries the sustaining step. It is a rival framework, not an established counterexample; Feser 2021 (also read) contests past-state sufficiency, and on the sustaining reading the dispute moves to conservation (q.104 a.1), which stays open. (b) The lead that an immaterial being cannot be present anywhere because presence requires location targets a spatial reading of presence that this bridge does not use (presence here is through causing being, q.8 a.1-2); no independent justification for it is on file, so it is a lead, not an objection. Strictly weaker than 'Whatever causes the being of everything else is IMMENSE_1' (its antecedent adds infinity; Control part 2: a cause of the being of all that is not infinite satisfies this bridge vacuously and falsifies the old one).
